correctness.rationale: Simultaneous diagonalization and inner product linear in first entry yield alpha_j=x_j conj(y_j), sum alpha=q and l1 sum <=1 by Cauchy-Schwarz. Conversely S=0 is realized by orthogonal standard vectors; S=1 by coordinate square roots; 0<S<1 with one active coordinate by an extra orthogonal x component, and with two or more by varying positive simplex t until sum |alpha_j|^2/t_j=1. Compactness and convexity follow from the affine section of the complex l1 ball. At the boundary, equality in triangle inequality forces each decomposition to share the same phase support; nontrivial perturbations exist iff columns (1,Re phase,Im phase) are real-linearly dependent. Thus extreme points have 2 or 3 active phases for |q|<1; |q|=1 becomes a simplex. An explicit three-phase sharpness vector (1+2r,(1-r)omega,(1-r)omega^2)*zeta/3 establishes necessary support three; independent complex arithmetic verified sums, l1 norm and nonzero area for r=0,.25,.75,.999. The convex hull of three-site compressions is claimed, not each value directly from a single compression. All m>=2, |q|<=1, compact Omega and continuous simultaneous diagonal family covered analytically.
